text:
alex_support: Heads up — escalated customer (prod) seeing streaming responses that cut off mid-JSON. No final finish_reason, last chunk is missing. Customer reports intermittent; they see the connection close shortly after last partial frame. Repro steps requested.
kevin_sre: Do we have raw SSE frames/logs? Is the client using HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1? Could be proxy coalescing or an idle timeout.
alex_support: Pasting the raw tail from the customer's capture (redacted):
```
data: {"id":"msg-x","object":"text_completion","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"...","finish_reason":null}]}
<socket closed by remote>
```
They say our SDK shows final tokens but their custom client does not see the final JSON chunk or the "[DONE]" event.
devon_engineer: Could be upstream runtime closed the socket before flush or an edge/HTTP proxy dropped the last TCP segment. Also seen with ALB/Nginx when keepalive/idle timeouts hit mid-stream and the final CRLF doesn't make it through. Any proxy (Fastly/Cloudflare) in front?
priya_support: Customer topology: internal app -> Cloudflare (spectrum) -> our API gateway (ALB) -> fastly -> runtime. They did confirm Cloudflare in front and use a Node fetch-based streamer in production. They said switching to our hosted JS SDK (ws fallback) reduces frequency but doesn't eliminate.
kevin_sre: Two quick repros to ask customer: 1) curl raw with --http1.1 and --http2 to compare. 2) use `nghttp` or `ncat` to capture the final bytes. Also ask for request headers. Example curl I sent them:
```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-large" --http2
```
alex_support: They ran the curl --http2 test and attached output: connection reset after final SSE frame, no trailing "data: [DONE]". When they forced --http1.1 it sometimes includes the final event. So HTTP/2 path looks suspect.
devon_engineer: That matches a Fastly/HTTP2 edge issue where stream resets can drop trailing chunk. Two mitigation paths: 1) make runtime send an explicit final empty event and double-flush on close, 2) suggest client-side retry/resume semantics. For immediate customer unblock, recommend forcing http1.1 or adding a short keepalive heartbeat to prevent edge idle close.
priya_support: Customer tried adding 1s heartbeats and saw fewer incidents. They asked if we can guarantee finish_reason emitted even on abrupt connection close — they rely on it for deterministic downstream processing.
kevin_sre: Internally: file a quick follow-up task for eng-runtime to ensure final flush on connection close and to add a finalization marker that is sent with TCP FIN-friendly framing. Also ask infra to audit ALB/fastly timeouts and config for long-lived SSE streams. I'll open an infra ticket.
support_bot: Ticket INC-2026 created and linked to T-2987. Assigned: eng-runtime (devon_engineer), SRE (kevin_sre). Priority: P1 until customer confirms stable.
alex_support: Sent customer the workaround steps: switch to http/1.1, add heartbeat, or use SDK streaming where we can coordinate retries. Requested tcpdump + raw frames + exact model + average token count for repro. Marking this thread until we get tcpdump.
kevin_sre: For repro checklist to include in ticket: model, prompt length, tokens/sec, region, full request/response headers, client library + version, exact proxy chain (Cloudflare/fastly/ALB), and whether connection used TLS session reuse. If they can provide pcap that shows the final FIN sequence that'd be ideal.
devon_engineer: Also trying a small server-side test: spawn a generation that delays final flush by 500ms and then force-close to see how edge handles tail bytes. If we can reproduce internally over same proxy chain config we can push a patch.
priya_support: Customer accepted workaround for now. They'll run the tcpdump and share. I'll update INC-2026 when we have captures. :thumbsup:
alex_support: Thanks — keeping P1 open until capture arrives.
